HARD RULES:
- /workspace holds the implementation under test. You are READ-ONLY on /workspace: never create, edit, or delete ANY file there. Do not run any command that writes into /workspace (no pip install -e, no flask db, no touching data-dev.sqlite).
- Write all of your own scratch files and test suites under your own private directory: WORKDIR below. mkdir -p it first.
- Run tests with:  cd WORKDIR && PYTHONPATH=/workspace python3 -m pytest -x -q <yourfile>   (or python3 -m unittest). Python is 3.9.23; Flask 0.12.2, Flask-SQLAlchemy 2.5.1, SQLAlchemy 1.4.46, Werkzeug 0.12.2, itsdangerous 0.24, WTForms 2.1, Flask-Login 0.4.0, Flask-HTTPAuth 3.2.3. Do NOT pip install anything.
- Use config name 'testing' (in-memory sqlite, CSRF disabled).
- ACTUALLY RUN every test you write. Never report a finding you have not reproduced with real output. Paste the real traceback into 'evidence'.
- Distinguish "the implementation is wrong" from "my test is wrong". If a test fails because of how YOU set it up (e.g. forgot db.create_all(), forgot Role.insert_roles(), forgot an app/request context), fix your test, do not report a finding.
- Report ONLY genuine defects in /workspace. If everything you tested passes, return an empty findings array. Empty is a perfectly good answer.


WORKDIR = /tmp/verify/packaging-verify


Key spec requirements to hold the implementation to:
- These imports must both work: `from flask import current_app` and
  `from app.models import User, Role, Post, Comment, create_app, db, fake, AnonymousUser, Permission, Follow`.
  `from app import ...` must also export all of those plus a version string.
- Permission bit flags: FOLLOW=1, COMMENT=2, WRITE=4, MODERATE=8, ADMIN=16.
- Roles from Role.insert_roles(): 'User' (default=True, FOLLOW|COMMENT|WRITE), 'Moderator' (+MODERATE), 'Administrator' (+ADMIN).
- Role: add_permission/remove_permission/reset_permissions/has_permission, __repr__ '<Role %r>'.
- User: password write-only property (reading raises AttributeError), verify_password, generate_confirmation_token/confirm,
  generate_reset_token/reset_password (static), generate_email_change_token/change_email, can, is_administrator, ping,
  gravatar_hash, gravatar, follow, unfollow, is_following, is_followed_by, followed_posts property, to_json,
  generate_auth_token, verify_auth_token (static), add_self_follows (static). User.__init__ self-follows.
- AnonymousUser.can() and .is_administrator() both return False; it is the login_manager.anonymous_user.
- Post.on_changed_body renders Markdown then bleach-cleans+linkifies into body_html; Post.to_json/from_json;
  from_json raises app.exceptions.ValidationError when body missing/empty. Same for Comment (narrower tag list).
- API mounted at /api/v1. Endpoints: GET users/<id>, users/<id>/posts/, users/<id>/timeline/, posts/, posts/<id>,
  POST posts/, PUT posts/<id>, GET comments/, comments/<id>, posts/<id>/comments/, POST posts/<id>/comments/, POST tokens/.
  HTTP Basic auth required on every API request (email+password, or auth token as username with empty password).
  Unauthenticated -> 401. Unconfirmed account -> 403. Collection responses carry keys posts/comments, prev, next, count.
- Web routes: main: / (GET+POST), /user/<username>, /edit-profile, /edit-profile/<int:id>, /post/<int:id> (GET+POST),
  /edit/<int:id>, /follow/<username>, /unfollow/<username>, /followers/<username>, /followed_by/<username>,
  /all, /followed, /moderate, /moderate/enable/<int:id>, /moderate/disable/<int:id>, /shutdown.
  auth (url_prefix /auth): /login, /logout, /register, /confirm/<token>, /confirm, /change-password, /reset,
  /reset/<token>, /change_email, /change_email/<token>, /unconfirmed.
- Anonymous GET / must return 200 and contain the word 'Stranger'.
- Forms: app/auth/forms.py -> LoginForm, RegistrationForm, ChangePasswordForm, PasswordResetRequestForm,
  PasswordResetForm, ChangeEmailForm. app/main/forms.py -> NameForm, EditProfileForm, EditProfileAdminForm,
  PostForm, CommentForm.
- app/decorators.py -> permission_required(permission), admin_required(f). app/api/decorators.py -> permission_required.
- app/email.py -> send_email(to, subject, template, **kwargs) returning the Thread, send_async_email(app, msg).
- app/api/errors.py -> bad_request/unauthorized/forbidden + a ValidationError handler on the api blueprint.


=== YOUR ASSIGNMENT ===
Another agent reviewed the Flasky implementation in /workspace and reported the finding below. Your job is to REFUTE it. Default to refuted=true unless you can independently reproduce the defect with your own freshly written test and your own reading of /workspace's source.

Reasons a finding should be REFUTED:
- You cannot reproduce it (paste what you actually ran and got).
- The "expected" behaviour is the reporter's invention, not something the specification or the upstream flasky project actually requires.
- The failure is an artifact of the reporter's test setup (missing db.create_all(), missing Role.insert_roles(), missing app/request context, Flask 0.12 test client lacking json=, etc.) rather than a defect in /workspace.
- It is a stylistic preference, a docs nit, or a "nice to have" with no behavioural consequence.

FINDING UNDER REVIEW:
title: No MANIFEST.in: sdist omits requirements.txt, so `pip install` of the sdist hard-fails during metadata generation
severity: high
file: MANIFEST.in
expected: `python3 setup.py sdist` should produce a self-contained source distribution, and `pip install flasky-1.0.0.tar.gz` should succeed offline, because setup.py declares requirements.txt as a build-time input.
actual: The sdist contains no requirements.txt, so `pip install <sdist>` dies with `FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.../requirements.txt'` at setup.py line 37 during `python setup.py egg_info`, before any code is installed.
evidence:
There is no MANIFEST.in in /workspace (`ls -la /workspace/MANIFEST.in` -> exit 2, no such file). setup.py calls requirements() at module import time (line 72: `install_requires=requirements()`), which reads requirements.txt (line 37: `for line in read('requirements.txt').splitlines():`). setuptools' default sdist manifest includes setup.py/README/LICENSE and .py files, but NOT requirements.txt.

Built the sdist from an unmodified copy of the tree:

  $ cd /tmp/verify/packaging/copy && python3 setup.py sdist --dist-dir /tmp/verify/packaging/dist
  ... Creating tar archive   (RC=0)

sdist contents (complete list, 37 entries) contain NO requirements.txt:
  flasky-1.0.0/LICENSE, PKG-INFO, README.md, config.py, flasky.py, setup.py, setup.cfg,
  flasky-1.0.0/app/*.py, app/api/*.py, app/auth/*.py, app/main/*.py,
  flasky-1.0.0/flasky.egg-info/*

Also confirmed via the generated manifest:
  $ grep -E 'templates|static|requirements' /tmp/verify/packaging/copy/flasky.egg-info/SOURCES.txt
  (no templates/static/requirements lines in SOURCES.txt)

Installing the extracted sdist offline fails:

  $ cd /tmp/verify/packaging/extract/flasky-1.0.0 && python3 -m pip install --no-deps --no-build-isolation --no-index --target /tmp/verify/packaging/sdist_site .
  Processing /tmp/verify/packaging/extract/flasky-1.0.0
    Preparing metadata (setup.py): started
    Preparing metadata (setup.py): finished with status 'error'
    error: subprocess-exited-with-error

    × python setup.py egg_info did not run successfully.
    │ exit code: 1
    ╰─> [10 lines of output]
        Traceback (most recent call last):
          File "<string>", line 2, in <module>
          File "<pip-setuptools-caller>", line 34, in <module>
          File "/tmp/verify/packaging/extract/flasky-1.0.0/setup.py", line 72, in <module>
            install_requires=requirements(),
          File "/tmp/verify/packaging/extract/flasky-1.0.0/setup.py", line 37, in requirements
            for line in read('requirements.txt').splitlines():
          File "/tmp/verify/packaging/extract/flasky-1.0.0/setup.py", line 20, in read
            with io.open(os.path.join(HERE, *parts), encoding='utf-8') as fh:
        FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/tmp/verify/packaging/extract/flasky-1.0.0/requirements.txt'
        [end of output]
  error: metadata-generation-failed
  PIP_RC=1

For contrast, installing directly from the source DIRECTORY works (pip copies the whole tree, so requirements.txt is present): that path produced flasky-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl size=44973 and installed successfully.

suggested_fix: Add a MANIFEST.in at the repo root that ships the build-time and data inputs, e.g.:

  include requirements.txt
  include LICENSE README.md Procfile Dockerfile docker-compose.yml boot.sh
  recursive-include app/templates *.html *.txt
  recursive-include app/static *
  recursive-include migrations *.py *.ini *.mako
  global-exclude *.pyc __pycache__

Optionally also harden setup.py's requirements() to degrade gracefully if requirements.txt is absent (wrap read() in a try/except IOError and fall back to a hardcoded list), so a malformed sdist cannot break metadata generation.

=== setup.py ===
#!/usr/bin/env python
"""Packaging for Flasky, the social blogging application.

Installing the project makes the :mod:`app` package (and the top level
``config`` / ``flasky`` modules) importable from anywhere::

    pip install -e .
"""

import io
import os
import re

from setuptools import setup, find_packages

HERE = os.path.abspath(os.path.dirname(__file__))


def read(*parts):
    with io.open(os.path.join(HERE, *parts), encoding='utf-8') as fh:
        return fh.read()


def find_version():
    match = re.search(r"^__version__ = ['\"]([^'\"]*)['\"]",
                      read('app', '__init__.py'), re.M)
    if match:
        return match.group(1)
    raise RuntimeError('Unable to find a version string in app/__init__.py')


def requirements():
    """Runtime dependencies, read straight out of ``requirements.txt``."""
    # Development-only tooling is deliberately left out of install_requires.
    skip = {'coverage', 'httpie', 'pytest', 'selenium', 'pygments'}
    reqs = []
    for line in read('requirements.txt').splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith('#'):
            continue
        name = re.split(r'[=<>!\[;]', line, 1)[0].strip().lower()
        if name in skip:
            continue
        reqs.append(line)
    return reqs


setup(
    name='flasky',
    version=find_version(),
    description='A social blogging application built with Flask.',
    long_description=read('README.md'),
    long_description_content_type='text/markdown',
    author='Flasky contributors',
    url='https://github.com/miguelgrinberg/flasky',
    license='MIT',
    packages=find_packages(exclude=['tests', 'tests.*', 'migrations',
                                    'migrations.*']),
    py_modules=['config', 'flasky'],
    include_package_data=True,
    package_data={
        'app': [
            'static/*',
            'templates/*.html',
            'templates/*/*.html',
            'templates/*/*.txt',
            'templates/*/*/*.html',
            'templates/*/*/*.txt',
        ],
    },
    zip_safe=False,
    install_requires=requirements(),
    python_requires='>=3.5',
    classifiers=[
        'Environment :: Web Environment',
        'Framework :: Flask',
        'Intended Audience :: Developers',
        'License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License',
        'Operating System :: OS Independent',
        'Programming Language :: Python',
        'Programming Language :: Python :: 3',
        'Topic :: Internet :: WWW/HTTP :: Dynamic Content',
    ],
)

## Installation

Clone the repository, create and activate a virtual environment, then install
the dependencies and the package itself:

```bash
python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate      # on Windows: venv\Scripts\activate

pip install -r requirements.txt
pip install -e .
```

Installing with `pip install -e .` puts the `app` package on the Python path in
editable mode, so changes to the source are picked up without reinstalling.

### Configuration

Configuration is read from environment variables (see `config.py`). The most
useful ones are:

| Variable | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `FLASK_APP` | Must be `flasky.py` for the `flask` CLI to find the app |
| `FLASK_CONFIG` | Configuration name: `development` (default), `testing`, `production`, `heroku`, `docker`, `unix` |
| `SECRET_KEY` | Secret used to sign sessions and tokens |

(a) Out of spec. Nothing in the specification mentions sdists, MANIFEST.in, PyPI publication, or `pip install <tarball>`. The only packaging-adjacent requirements are the import/export contracts, and they all pass. The repo never claims to ship an sdist. /workspace/README.md "Installation" (lines ~151-164) documents exactly one path: clone the repo, `pip install -r requirements.txt`, `pip install -e .`, and states "Installing with `pip install -e .` puts the `app` package on the Python path in editable mode". setup.py's own module docstring says the same (`pip install -e .`). No fix required for spec compliance — the documented install path (`pip install -r requirements.txt` + `pip install -e .` from a clone, per /workspace/README.md lines ~151-164 and the setup.py docstring) works, and a wheel built from the tree installs and serves `GET / -> 200` with templates intact from an isolated site dir.

A correct MANIFEST.in at /workspace/MANIFEST.in would need both the build input and the data files:

  include requirements.txt
  include LICENSE README.md Procfile Dockerfile docker-compose.yml boot.sh
  recursive-include app/templates *.html *.txt
  recursive-include app/static *
  recursive-include migrations *.py *.ini *.mako
  global-exclude *.pyc __pycache__

and, defensively, /workspace/setup.py `requirements()` (line 37) could wrap `read('requirements.txt')` in `try/except (IOError, OSError)` returning a hardcoded fallback list so a malformed sdist degrades instead of failing metadata generation. Both are optional packaging hygiene with no effect on any behaviour the specification requires.
